Hi, is there a way to just get 1 snippet worth HTML full code for Verso, which I could insert in my html files for website, etc.. This would have hover feature with goals showing like usual Verso code.
I spend some long hours to create a set of script which if i gave a Lean code (no Verso imports etc), it spat out 1 html code for it, which you can insert anywhere with iframe in your html or markdown files
I would like to know if this is a simpler way. Having code snippets html would be very useful I believe

If not, I would love to share what I made so that everyone can use it(need to format it in a presentable way have made a repo).
Here is a dummy example for how that looks like.
demo-1.html

Repo i made: https://github.com/AnirudhG07/verso-snippets
If there is a better workaround, great(please share). Otherwise I hope this helps.

For this task, I'd use SubVerso, the code rendering library that Verso calls out to. SubVerso has a few things that make it relevant here:

  • Broad version compatibility - it's tested against all Lean releases back to 4.0.0. This means that you can re-render your blog post if needed without having to update the code samples, assuming you can still run that Lean version on your computer or in a container or VM.
  • Code sample extraction - it supports the "anchor" syntax from mdbook's Rust processing. This means you can name snippets of the code, and it can pull them out with full information, so you can refer e.g. to three lines in a program, or to a proof state at a particular location.
  • No imports needed - it drives the Lean compiler through its API to produce its JSON intermediate format.

Verso itself can be used to make the HTML from the JSON. There isn't ready-made scripts for this, but presumably that's what you've implemented :-) I wouldn't use an iframe for this though, but rather just stick the HTML in directly (perhaps as a comment substitution function?). That avoids iframe weirdness. But presumably there's a good reason for doing it this way - can you say more?
I just use iframe to plugin the HTML file I made for Lean code into somewhere else. Thats all. You can also do it other ways.

The way I have implemented is kind of hacky. You take the code snippet and put it in a usual Verso file. Create the set of Html files which Verso makes, and extract out the html file relevant, and package it into 1 html code.

I see that the code is creating a full-blown Verso document, then extracting the text via Python. This clearly works - but I'd encourage you to work at the level of calling SubVerso to extract the JSON (this is just a matter of adding a dependency and then building a Lake facet), and then write a small Lean executable that uses Verso's HTML-generation library to read the JSON and dump suitable HTML. This should be a pretty short program, and I suspect it will be more robust in the face of Verso changes and updates, and it gives you a way to keep old example code building that's written in a mix of Lean versions while still benefiting from improvements made in Verso itself.

Hi @Anirudh Gupta , Verso Blueprint does have functionality like the one I think you are wondering in your first post, indeed the goal is to be able to insert blueprint nodes in other websites. This goes a bit beyond of Subverso, and could be useful for you or not.

See https://leanprover.github.io/verso-blueprint/js-api/

The way it works is that VBP will save a .json cache, then the JS API re-renders from that.

I think it'd be interesting to make this a more general Verso mechanism, but we'll have to wait for @David Thrane Christiansen to be back.

Meanwhile the way it is done in Verso Blueprint could be useful for you as a reference.

Regarding richer infoview support, as far as I can tell there is nothing more detailed right now than what you get from subverso. It could be tricky to imitate the proofview well as it is a dynamic component and will call Lean LSP server often to enrich the view.
Thanks, ill check that out.
